content:
This is perhaps part of a much wider discussion for the whole ecosystem, but we need to decide how to avoid having different contributors work on the same roadmap targets!

See in particular @Michael R Douglas's comment at https://github.com/FormalFrontier/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/16#issuecomment-4763112528, where he proposes a split in the work for the OneParameterSemigroups roadmap.

(For now, I'm just running some workers which randomly select from all available roadmaps when they have completed their review duties and have capacity for working on new content: this is the default behaviour ./tauceti work and ./tauceti work --loop. This is intentionally a shot-gun approach to force us to learn how to deal with these issues!)

I propose:

  1. I will add a --roadmap-skip flag, to go along with --roadmap-focus flag (which I think I will rename to --roadmap-only)
  2. I will restart my workers with ./tauceti work --loop --roadmap-skip OneParameterSemigroups, to at least temporarily avoid contention with @Michael R Douglas's workers by doing nothing
  3. We then implement a claim sharing mechanism so it's actually possible to follow Michael's suggested division of labour. (I don't particularly care what my workers work on for now: I just want to get these coordination issues sorted.)

Now, that claim sharing mechanism... We also need to build a progress reporting mechanism, so it one can programmatically inspect a roadmap and determine which parts of it are complete. (Blueprints! There's lots of existing technology here, but I want to move slowly and introduce this as needed, and make sure we do so via orthogonal tools, so we don't end up with a huge spaghetti monster driving Tau Ceti)

So I propose for now we leave progress reporting, and its interaction with claim sharing, as out of scope. (Hopefully not for long!)

I propose that we use the existing claim-bot mechanism, built by @Pietro Monticone and @Shreyas Srinivas, and already used in PNT+, Equational Theories, FLT, and infinity-cosmos. I'll investigate now turning claim-bot into a reusable github action (currently it just has four copy-pasted implementations across those libraries...) and adding support for automatic expiry of claims based on user-specifiable/project-defaultable expiry dates.

Once that is set up, we can work out how to feed information from the claims records into worker agents. I think it's important that we plan this is always "best effort": people are still welcome to contribute to Tau Ceti even if they completely ignore the claims mechanism!

@Michael R Douglas okay, I think I have a decent first prototype for claiming/assigning tasks. I've invited you as a "collaborator" to the repository. If you accept that invitation, we'll test things out with your proposed division of labour for that roadmap.
We're now using the leanprover-community/intentions setup, as described at #Project announcements > leanprover-community/intentions.

This seems to be working, and the ./tauceti work (and specifically the --only roadmap branch of the work command) is now fed information about any relevant issues on the TauCetiRoadmap repository that are subject to claims using the leanprover-community/intentions machinery.

Michael and I have each registered a claim on parts of the OneParameterSemigroups roadmap, and it seems like the agents respect these. But... much more testing in production is required.

Everyone is invited to exercise this mechanism. :-)

If/when people implement alternative workers, if they want to participate in this intentions registration mechanism, they should look for roadmap/X labelled issues at TauCetiRoadmap, after they've decided to work on roadmap X, and read these issues and the assignees (checking the assignees against whoever they are operated by/for), and take this into account when deciding which items in that roadmap to work on.
